Scoring Misère: Two Heaps

Game Strategy

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)

Game: two heaps of chips. Take 1 up to Max move from one heap. Whoever takes the last chip loses.
How to play: click the leftmost chip you want to remove — that chip and everything to its right come off.
Look for the math

With exactly two heaps, misère Scoring has a perfect strategy — Kalman and Keynes’s “Double Take” in Math Horizons, extended on the page to any Max move M ≥ 2.

When the second player wins

Write residues mod M+1. Second player wins with best play precisely when the sizes are congruent to (0,1) or (1,0), or both congruent to the same k with 2 ≤ k ≤ M. The logic test checks this formula against an exhaustive search on every pair up to size 12 for M = 2…5.

Why packages of M+1

After a take of t from a tall heap, the opponent can answer with M+1−t from the same heap, removing a full package. So only the residues matter — until the endgame where one heap is empty and the other has a single chip, forcing the next player to take the last.

The computer

The applet’s MakeMoveFromEqual / MakeMoveFromDifferent implement that pairing strategy (with a few random choices among equally good replies). Play from a second-player-win opening and try to catch it out.

With Max move 3, try heaps 4 and 1 — that is a second-player win.
